elements.description: Synchronously delivers an event to every eligible generic extension handler. The engine accepts arbitrary event hashes and opaque payloads without event or payload registration. Receivers ignore event ids they do not recognize. Use extension-specific names for custom events; names beginning with _dm_event_ are reserved for engine events. This function is not thread-safe. Call only on the engine thread. Callbacks run on the calling thread; no queuing or worker-thread marshalling occurs. Nested dispatch is supported. Delivery order is unspecified; events cannot be consumed. The context registry and payload are borrowed until return. Each broadcast supplies callback parameters using the registry's contexts and each receiver's user data. Event parameters have a delta time of zero. The sender retains ownership. Data is read-only to receivers. Passing null data with data_size zero sends a payload-free event. The engine forwards the payload without interpreting its contents.
elements.examples:
HContextRegistry context_registry = ParamsGetContextRegistry(params);
uint32_t value = 42;
BroadcastEvent(context_registry, dmHashString64("my_extension.changed"), &value, sizeof(value));

elements.description:
Declare an extension using its identifier and register/unregister
callbacks. The identifier is also its exported registration symbol and name.
Register configures lifecycle callbacks on the opaque extension handle, before
AppInitialize. Unregister runs after AppFinalize. Both repeat on engine reboot.
The legacy eight-argument form remains supported and emits a compiler
deprecation warning: DM_DECLARE_EXTENSION(symbol, name, app_init, app_final,
init, update, on_event, final). It keeps its callbacks and ABI. Do not add new
callbacks to that form; use setters through the three-argument form.
elements.examples:
static ExtensionResult RegisterMyExtension(HExtension extension)
{
    ExtensionSetUpdateFn(extension, UpdateMyExtension);
    return EXTENSION_RESULT_OK;
}
DM_DECLARE_EXTENSION(MyExtension, RegisterMyExtension, 0);

elements.description: Register an iOS application delegate for process-level callbacks such as launch and remote notification registration. Multiple delegates are supported (Max 32). Use application:willFinishLaunchingWithOptions: and application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: for launch. The older applicationDidFinishLaunching: callback is not synthesized. Defold uses the UIScene lifecycle. Application activity, URL and user activity callbacks are not forwarded from scenes; use ExtensionRegisteriOSUISceneDelegate. The game window is created after application launch. Use scene connection to access it, and scene connection options for cold-launch URLs and user activities. application:supportedInterfaceOrientationsForWindow: can override the game's orientation settings, including on iOS 27 and later. The last nonzero mask containing only valid UIInterfaceOrientationMask bits in delegate dispatch order is used. Invalid masks are ignored. The application, scene, and root view controller share this policy, including during full-screen presentations. The game's default mask comes from the DefoldSupportedInterfaceOrientations Info.plist array, with DefoldSupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad taking precedence on iPad. If neither contains usable orientations, Defold falls back to UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad on iPad, then UISupportedInterfaceOrientations. Arrays contain UIKit orientation names such as UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait. The default policy excludes upside-down portrait on iPhone. If no array is usable, all device-supported orientations are allowed. The built-in manifest keeps the UIKit arrays broad and uses the Defold array for the game's orientation settings. UIKit may ignore orientation restrictions, including on iPhone Duo's inner display. Games must still handle window size changes. Register before scene connection to affect the initial orientation. To update the policy after scene connection, call setNeedsUpdateOfSupportedInterfaceOrientations on the root view controller (iOS 16+) or attemptRotationToDeviceOrientation (iOS 15).
elements.name: ExtensionRegisteriOSUIApplicationDelegate
notes:
Register before UIApplicationMain to receive launch callbacks. Registration
does not retain the delegate; keep it alive until it is unregistered.
This function is only available on iOS. [icon:ios]

elements.description:
Register an iOS scene observer. Multiple delegates are supported (Max 32).
Defold owns the single game window and its scene configuration. Registered
observers receive scene connection/disconnection, activation/deactivation,
foreground/background, openURLContexts, continueUserActivity,
willContinueUserActivityWithType, didFailToContinueUserActivityWithType:error:
and didUpdateUserActivity callbacks. Other optional delegate methods are not
forwarded. No legacy UIApplicationDelegate callbacks are synthesized.
Register before UIApplicationMain (for example in a static constructor) to
receive the initial scene connection. Extension app-initialize is too late.
Cold-launch URLs, user activities and notification responses are available in
UISceneConnectionOptions. Scene connection may precede Lua initialization;
extensions must retain any data they need to deliver to Lua later.
elements.examples:
// myextension_ios.mm
@interface MySceneDelegate : NSObject <UISceneDelegate>
- (void)scene:(UIScene*)scene willConnectToSession:(UISceneSession*)session options:(UISceneConnectionOptions*)options;
- (void)scene:(UIScene*)scene openURLContexts:(NSSet<UIOpenURLContext*>*)contexts;
@end

struct MySceneDelegateRegistration
{
    MySceneDelegate* m_Delegate;
    MySceneDelegateRegistration()
    {
        m_Delegate = [[MySceneDelegate alloc] init];
        dmExtension::RegisteriOSUISceneDelegate(m_Delegate);
    }
    ~MySceneDelegateRegistration()
    {
        dmExtension::UnregisteriOSUISceneDelegate(m_Delegate);
        [m_Delegate release];
    }
};
MySceneDelegateRegistration g_MySceneDelegateRegistration;
elements.name: ExtensionRegisteriOSUISceneDelegate
notes:
Register and unregister on the main thread. Registration does not retain
the delegate; keep it alive until unregistering. Each event retains a snapshot
of its observers, so unregistering during delivery affects subsequent events.
Duplicate registrations are ignored. Late registration does not replay events.
This function is only available on iOS. [icon:ios]

elements.description: Synchronous delivery on the engine thread, after successful AppInitialize (or when it is omitted) until that extension's AppFinalize begins. Engine Initialize is not required: window events and cleanup after a failed initialization may have partial contexts. Engine-owned registry entries are cleared as their contexts are destroyed; Lua and resource-factory parameters can be null during application finalization. Event dispatch is not thread-safe. Publish events only on the engine thread. Callbacks run synchronously on the calling thread; dispatch does not marshal calls from worker threads. Nested dispatch on the same engine thread is supported. One catch-all callback receives every generic event. Parameters and data are borrowed for this call only. Inspect event_id to choose which events to handle; no per-event registration is required. Payload-free events pass null data and data_size zero. Receivers interpret data according to the event's documented payload type and size. Delivery order between extensions is unspecified. All events are broadcasts; every eligible handler is called and events cannot be consumed. Extensions can publish custom events through BroadcastEvent. Ignore ids you do not recognize. Built-in engine event definitions are available in <dmsdk/engine/engine_event.h>.

elements.description:
Call only from the register callback. One handler receives all generic
events; use the callback's event_id to select events. No event-name argument
or per-event registration is needed. Passing null clears it.
Registration resets on engine reboot; no event is replayed to a late receiver.
elements.name: SetEventFn

elements.name: SetInitializeFn

elements.description:
Call only from the register callback. Passing null clears the callback.
Delivery requires successful AppInitialize, or no AppInitialize callback, and
stops before AppFinalize. It does not require an Initialize callback.
elements.name: SetPostRenderFn

elements.description:
Call only from the register callback. Passing null clears the callback.
Delivery requires successful AppInitialize, or no AppInitialize callback, and
stops before AppFinalize. It does not require an Initialize callback.
elements.name: SetPreRenderFn

elements.description:
Call only from the register callback. Passing null clears the callback.
Updates begin after successful engine initialization and stop before Finalize,
even when no Initialize or Finalize callback is configured.
elements.name: SetUpdateFn

elements.brief: associate user data with an extension
elements.description:
Call only from the register callback. The engine borrows this pointer;
it does not allocate, copy or free the memory. Passing null clears it.
Retrieve it from callback parameters with ParamsGetUserData or
AppParamsGetUserData, and from the unregister callback with
GetUserData. Keep it valid through all callbacks, then release
it in unregister. If registration fails, release it before returning because
unregister is not called. The pointer resets to null before each registration
and after unregister, including engine reboot.
elements.name: SetUserData
